# Potential gains and vmPFC activity

## Question and result

**Does the gain-related response increase with potential gain in the equal-indifference group?** The prespecified test is a positive one-sample group effect of the AO86 participant gain cope maps. [FINAL_RESULT]

## Analysis

We analyzed the 54 supplied equal-indifference participant maps. The input manifest checksums, byte counts, participant IDs, finite values, and common image geometry were verified before inference. No maps were excluded. A common-coverage whole-brain mask was defined as voxels with nonzero finite estimates in all 54 maps.

The primary model was a one-sample group test of the positive mean cope. Family-wise error was controlled across the whole common mask using a one-sided sign-flip permutation test with TFCE and 10,000 permutations (seed 20261015; α = .05). The hypothesis is supported only if the corrected map contains positive significant voxels in the vmPFC region. This follows the original NARPS instruction to report whole-brain analyses, not region-only tests ([NARPS analysis instructions](https://www.narps.info/files/narps_instructions_for_analysis_teams.pdf)).

The anatomical vmPFC summary used bilateral medial orbitofrontal parcels (AAL3, `Frontal_Med_Orb_L/R`) resampled by nearest neighbor to the participant-map grid, then intersected with common coverage. This is a prespecified anatomical operationalization rather than a data-selected cluster. We report the participants' average cope in this ROI and its t-based 95% interval descriptively; the ROI result does not replace whole-brain correction. The medial orbitofrontal cortex is a common anatomical approximation to vmPFC in analyses of NARPS hypotheses, for which the original hypothesis did not specify a coordinate or atlas ROI ([NARPS analysis discussion](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10233921/); [AAL3 atlas](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2019.116189)).

## Findings

[FINDINGS]

![Group effect and whole-brain inference](figures/gain_group_inference.png)

![One-sample t map with medial orbitofrontal ROI outline](figures/gain_tmap_vmPFC.png)

## Interpretation and limits

These images are participant-level contrast parameter estimates (copes), not standardized test statistics or currency-unit slopes. Upstream, the gain modulator was mean-centered and variance-normalized before HRF convolution, responses were modeled with response-time durations, and gain and loss were entered in separate models. The estimated effect therefore describes the response to that normalized gain modulator conditional on those fixed modeling choices; it cannot be read as BOLD change per dollar, and this analysis does not separate gain coding from consequences of the upstream model specification.

No participant variance maps were supplied. The group test is an unweighted one-sample analysis of participant copes, not a precision-weighted mixed-effects model that propagates first-level uncertainty. Sign-flip inference also assumes exchangeability under sign changes (in particular, a sufficiently symmetric null distribution of participant effects). The 10,000 sampled permutations give Monte Carlo, not exhaustive, inference.

If the whole-brain test does not support the hypothesis, that means these data and this group model do not establish a positive gain effect after whole-brain family-wise correction. It does not show that the effect is exactly zero or that vmPFC never tracks potential gains; smaller, spatially diffuse, or more variable effects may not be detected. Atlas boundaries and the MNI152-to-MNI2009cAsym resampling also make the ROI summary approximate.

## Reproducibility

Run from the repository root with `pixi run python scripts/analyze_gain.py`. The script validates the inputs, runs the group model, writes the NIfTI maps and figures, and saves machine-readable results in `results/results.json`. The complete command, captured output, resource samples, and run summary are under `logs/`.

.. _aal_atlas:

AAL atlas
=========

Access
------
See :func:`nilearn.datasets.fetch_atlas_aal`.

Notes
-----
This :term:`Deterministic atlas` is the result of an automated anatomical :term:`parcellation`
of the spatially normalized single-subject high-resolution T1 volume
provided by the Montreal Neurological Institute (:term:`MNI`)
(:footcite:t:`Collins1998`).

Using this :term:`parcellation` method, three procedures to perform the automated anatomical labeling
of functional studies are proposed:
(1) labeling of an extremum defined by a set of coordinates,
(2) percentage of voxels belonging to each of the AVOI intersected by a sphere centered by a set of coordinates, and
(3) percentage of voxels belonging to each of the AVOI intersected by an activated cluster.

For the AAL version SPM 5, 8, and 12, the map image (data.maps) contains 117 unique integer values
that define the parcellation.
However, these values are not consecutive integers from 0 to 116, as is usually the case in Nilearn.
Therefore, they should not be interpreted as indices for the list of label names.

In contrast, the total number of parcellations in AAL 3v2 is 167.
The 3v2 atlas contains 171 unique integer values that define the parcellation.
These values are consecutive integers from 0 to 170,
except for the anterior cingulate cortex (35, 36) and thalamus (81, 82), which are left empty in AAL 3v2.
In addition, the region IDs are provided as strings, so it is necessary to cast them to integers when indexing.

For example, with version SPM 5, 8 and 12, to get the name of the region
corresponding to the region ID 5021 in the image, you should do:

.. code-block:: python

    # This should print 'Lingual_L'
    data.labels[data.indices.index("5021")]

Conversely, to get the region ID corresponding to the label
"Precentral_L", you should do:

.. code-block:: python

    # This should print '2001'
    data.indices[data.labels.index("Precentral_L")]

For more information on this dataset's structure, see
https://www.gin.cnrs.fr/en/tools/aal/, :footcite:t:`AAL_atlas`,
and :footcite:t:`Tzourio-Mazoyer2002`.

Content
-------
    :"maps": :obj:`str`. path to nifti file containing regions.
    :"labels": dict. labels dictionary with their region id as key and name as value
    :"indices": :obj:`list` of :obj:`str` Indices mapping 'labels' to values in the 'maps' image.
    :"lut": look up table for the regions

References
----------

.. footbibliography::

License
-------

-The anatomical vmPFC summary used bilateral medial orbitofrontal parcels (AAL3, `Frontal_Med_Orb_L/R`) resampled by nearest neighbor to the participant-map grid, then intersected with common coverage. This is a prespecified anatomical operationalization rather than a data-selected cluster. We report the participants' average cope in this ROI and its t-based 95% interval descriptively; the ROI result does not replace whole-brain correction. The medial orbitofrontal cortex is a common anatomical approximation to vmPFC in analyses of NARPS hypotheses, for which the original hypothesis did not specify a coordinate or atlas ROI ([NARPS analysis discussion](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10233921/); [AAL3 atlas](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2019.116189)).
+The anatomical vmPFC summary used bilateral medial orbitofrontal parcels (`Frontal_Med_Orb_L/R`) from the AAL SPM12 atlas, resampled by nearest neighbor to the participant-map grid and intersected with common coverage. This is a fixed anatomical operationalization rather than a data-selected cluster. A published NARPS reanalysis similarly operationalized vmPFC with medial orbitofrontal parcels, while noting that the original hypothesis did not specify an atlas ROI ([NARPS analysis discussion](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10233921/)). We report the participants' average cope and t-based 95% interval descriptively; this ROI result does not replace whole-brain correction ([AAL atlas](https://doi.org/10.1006/nimg.2001.0978)).

# Potential gains and vmPFC activity

## Question and result

**We found no support for a positive gain-related response in the vmPFC.** In the predefined bilateral medial orbitofrontal ROI, the mean participant cope was −0.0079 (95% t interval −0.0346 to 0.0188; 54 participants; descriptive one-sided t = −0.60, p = .723). No whole-brain FWE-significant voxel overlapped the ROI. The whole-brain max-t test detected 24 positive voxels in three small posterior patches (peak t = 6.62 at MNI [−26, −102, −3.6]; minimum corrected p = .00050). These posterior findings do not support the vmPFC hypothesis.

## Analysis

We analyzed the 54 supplied equal-indifference participant maps. The input manifest checksums, byte counts, participant IDs, finite values, and common image geometry were verified before inference. No maps were excluded. A common-coverage whole-brain mask was defined as voxels with nonzero finite estimates in all 54 maps.

The primary model was a one-sample group test of the positive mean cope. Family-wise error was controlled across the whole common mask using a one-sided sign-flip permutation max-t test and 10,000 permutations (seed 20261015; α = .05). The hypothesis is supported only if the corrected map contains positive significant voxels in the vmPFC region. This follows the original NARPS instruction to report whole-brain analyses, not region-only tests ([NARPS analysis instructions](https://www.narps.info/files/narps_instructions_for_analysis_teams.pdf)).

The anatomical vmPFC summary used bilateral medial orbitofrontal parcels (`Frontal_Med_Orb_L/R`) from the AAL SPM12 atlas, resampled by nearest neighbor to the participant-map grid and intersected with common coverage. This is a fixed anatomical operationalization rather than a data-selected cluster. A published NARPS reanalysis similarly operationalized vmPFC with medial orbitofrontal parcels, while noting that the original hypothesis did not specify an atlas ROI ([NARPS analysis discussion](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10233921/)). We report the participants' average cope and t-based 95% interval descriptively; this ROI result does not replace whole-brain correction ([AAL atlas](https://doi.org/10.1006/nimg.2001.0978)).

## Findings

[FINDINGS]

![Group effect and whole-brain inference](figures/gain_group_inference.png)

![One-sample t map at vmPFC. Cyan outlines the medial orbitofrontal ROI; magenta marks voxels surviving whole-brain correction. The map uses an uncorrected display threshold.](figures/gain_tmap_vmPFC.png)

![Positive whole-brain voxels surviving max-t family-wise correction](figures/gain_fwe_significant_map.png)

## Interpretation and limits

These images are participant-level contrast parameter estimates (copes), not standardized test statistics or currency-unit slopes. Upstream, the gain modulator was mean-centered and variance-normalized before HRF convolution, responses were modeled with response-time durations, and gain and loss were entered in separate models. The estimated effect therefore describes the response to that normalized gain modulator conditional on those fixed modeling choices; it cannot be read as BOLD change per dollar, and this analysis does not separate gain coding from consequences of the upstream model specification.

No participant variance maps were supplied. The group test is an unweighted one-sample analysis of participant copes, not a precision-weighted mixed-effects model that propagates first-level uncertainty. Sign-flip inference also assumes exchangeability under sign changes (in particular, a sufficiently symmetric null distribution of participant effects). The 10,000 sampled permutations give Monte Carlo, not exhaustive, inference. A slower TFCE permutation attempt was interrupted for runtime; its duct logs are retained, and it is not used for the reported inference.

The absence of corrected vmPFC voxels means these data and this group model do not establish a positive gain effect in that region after whole-brain family-wise correction. It does not show that the effect is exactly zero or that vmPFC never tracks potential gains; smaller, spatially diffuse, or more variable effects may not be detected. The uncorrected ROI p-value is descriptive and is not evidence for or against the whole-brain-corrected hypothesis. Atlas boundaries and the MNI152-to-MNI2009cAsym resampling also make the ROI summary approximate.

## Reproducibility

Run from the repository root with `pixi run python scripts/analyze_gain.py`. # Potential gains and vmPFC activity

## Question and result

**We found no support for a positive gain-related response in the vmPFC.** In the predefined bilateral medial orbitofrontal ROI, the mean participant cope was −0.0079 (95% t interval −0.0346 to 0.0188; 54 participants; descriptive one-sided t = −0.60, p = .723). No whole-brain FWE-significant voxel overlapped the ROI. The whole-brain max-t test detected 24 positive voxels in three small posterior patches (peak t = 6.62 at MNI [−26, −102, −3.6]; minimum corrected p = .00050). These posterior findings do not support the vmPFC hypothesis.

## Analysis

We analyzed the 54 supplied equal-indifference participant maps. The input manifest checksums, byte counts, participant IDs, finite values, and common image geometry were verified before inference. No maps were excluded. A common-coverage whole-brain mask was defined as voxels with nonzero finite estimates in all 54 maps.

The primary model was a one-sample group test of the positive mean cope. Family-wise error was controlled across the whole common mask using a one-sided sign-flip permutation max-t test and 10,000 permutations (seed 20261015; α = .05). The hypothesis is supported only if the corrected map contains positive significant voxels in the vmPFC region. This follows the original NARPS instruction to report whole-brain analyses, not region-only tests ([NARPS analysis instructions](https://www.narps.info/files/narps_instructions_for_analysis_teams.pdf)).

The anatomical vmPFC summary used bilateral medial orbitofrontal parcels (`Frontal_Med_Orb_L/R`) from the AAL SPM12 atlas, resampled by nearest neighbor to the participant-map grid and intersected with common coverage. This is a fixed anatomical operationalization rather than a data-selected cluster. A published NARPS reanalysis similarly operationalized vmPFC with medial orbitofrontal parcels, while noting that the original hypothesis did not specify an atlas ROI ([NARPS analysis discussion](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10233921/)). We report the participants' average cope and t-based 95% interval descriptively; this ROI result does not replace whole-brain correction ([AAL atlas](https://doi.org/10.1006/nimg.2001.0978)).

## Findings

[FINDINGS]

![Group effect and whole-brain inference](figures/gain_group_inference.png)

![One-sample t map at vmPFC. Cyan outlines the medial orbitofrontal ROI; magenta marks voxels surviving whole-brain correction. The map uses an uncorrected display threshold.](figures/gain_tmap_vmPFC.png)

![Positive whole-brain voxels surviving max-t family-wise correction](figures/gain_fwe_significant_map.png)

## Interpretation and limits

These images are participant-level contrast parameter estimates (copes), not standardized test statistics or currency-unit slopes. Upstream, the gain modulator was mean-centered and variance-normalized before HRF convolution, responses were modeled with response-time durations, and gain and loss were entered in separate models. The estimated effect therefore describes the response to that normalized gain modulator conditional on those fixed modeling choices; it cannot be read as BOLD change per dollar, and this analysis does not separate gain coding from consequences of the upstream model specification.

No participant variance maps were supplied. The group test is an unweighted one-sample analysis of participant copes, not a precision-weighted mixed-effects model that propagates first-level uncertainty. Sign-flip inference also assumes exchangeability under sign changes (in particular, a sufficiently symmetric null distribution of participant effects). The 10,000 sampled permutations give Monte Carlo, not exhaustive, inference. A slower TFCE permutation attempt was interrupted for runtime; its duct logs are retained, and it is not used for the reported inference.

The absence of corrected vmPFC voxels means these data and this group model do not establish a positive gain effect in that region after whole-brain family-wise correction. It does not show that the effect is exactly zero or that vmPFC never tracks potential gains; smaller, spatially diffuse, or more variable effects may not be detected. The uncorrected ROI p-value is descriptive and is not evidence for or against the whole-brain-corrected hypothesis. Atlas boundaries and the MNI152-to-MNI2009cAsym resampling also make the ROI summary approximate.

## Reproducibility

Run from the repository root with `pixi run python scripts/analyze_gain.py`. The script validates the inputs, runs the group model, writes the NIfTI maps and figures, and saves machine-readable results in `results/results.json`. The complete command, captured output, resource samples, and run summary are under `logs/`.
